## 2026-08-18T07:33:26.765Z
- Item: issue #4546 — source map with `deleteAfterUpload` doesn't strip sourcemap comments from css files
- Conclusion: Confirmed scope gap in the Turbopack sourcemap-comment cleanup: it only processes JavaScript files, so dangling CSS source map references remain after deletion.
- Labels: feature/error-tracking, team/error-tracking
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4546
- Relevant files: `packages/nextjs-config/src/config.ts`, `packages/nextjs-config/src/strip-sourcemap-comments.ts`, `packages/nextjs-config/src/strip-sourcemap-comments.spec.ts`, `packages/nextjs-config/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/webpack-plugin/src/index.ts`
- Findings: `withCompilerConfig` calls `stripDanglingSourceMapComments` after sourcemap upload only when Turbopack is enabled and `deleteAfterUpload` is true.; `stripDanglingSourceMapComments` currently calls `listJsFiles`, whose extension filter is limited to `.js`, `.mjs`, and `.cjs`; no `.css` assets are inspected.; The current matcher only recognizes JavaScript line comments (`//# sourceMappingURL=...`), not CSS block comments (`/*# sourceMappingURL=... */`).; The existing tests cover JavaScript cleanup, retained existing maps, inline maps, remote maps, CRLF, and module extensions, but contain no CSS fixture.; `packages/nextjs-config/CHANGELOG.md` confirms #3764 shipped in 1.9.68 specifically as a Turbopack dangling-comment cleanup.; The webpack plugin already suppresses SourceMapDevToolPlugin comment emission with `append: false` when `deleteAfterUpload` is enabled, but it separately deletes emitted CSS map files after upload.
- Fix assessment: The omission is localized to the Next.js Turbopack cleanup helper. A small extension to inspect CSS files and remove only dangling local CSS mapping comments, backed by focused tests, addresses the reported behavior without changing upload or deletion semantics.
- PR: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/pull/4547

## 2026-08-18T08:31:39.416Z
- Item: issue #3205 — Remove source maps from distribution
- Conclusion: Valid distribution-size enhancement: posthog-js currently publishes generated source maps, which can substantially inflate node_modules and production container images even if they are not included in the client bundle.
- Labels: enhancement, web, feature, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/3205
- Relevant files: `packages/browser/package.json`, `packages/browser/rollup.config.mjs`, `packages/browser/scripts/check-sourcemap-ignore-list.js`, `packages/browser/scripts/check-mangled-property-consistency.js`
- Findings: `packages/browser/rollup.config.mjs` sets `sourcemap: true` for every generated browser entrypoint, so the build emits source-map artifacts into `dist/`.; `packages/browser/package.json` publishes `dist/*`, which includes `.js.map` files alongside JavaScript and declaration outputs.; The browser package's post-build checks deliberately consume generated maps: `check-sourcemap-ignore-list.js` requires source maps to exist, and `check-mangled-property-consistency.js` reads maps to validate cross-bundle property mangling.; Therefore, source maps should be retained through build and validation, then excluded only from the npm tarball rather than disabled globally.
- Fix assessment: The requested behavior is isolated to npm package contents. It does not require changing runtime code or disabling source-map generation used by existing build checks.

## 2026-08-19T13:55:13.093Z
- Item: issue #4566 — PostHogErrorBoundary drops componentStack from the captured exception event
- Conclusion: Confirmed @posthog/react bug: React's component stack is available at both React error-capture call sites but is not included in the captured exception properties.
- Labels: feature/error-tracking, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4566
- Relevant files: `packages/react/src/components/PostHogErrorBoundary.tsx`, `packages/react/src/components/__tests__/PostHogErrorBoundary.test.tsx`, `packages/react/src/helpers/error-helpers.ts`, `packages/browser/src/posthog-core.ts`, `packages/types/src/posthog.ts`, `packages/core/src/error-tracking/error-properties-builder.ts`
- Findings: `PostHogErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch(error, errorInfo)` calls `additionalProperties(error)` and `client.captureException(error, currentProperties)`, then stores `errorInfo.componentStack` solely in component state for the fallback.; `setupReactErrorHandler` receives `(error, errorInfo)` but calls `client.captureException(error)` before passing `errorInfo` only to its optional callback.; The public `captureException(error, additionalProperties?)` API accepts arbitrary additional event properties, and the browser implementation merges those properties into the generated exception payload before sending it. This permits a React-specific component-stack property without modifying the core exception builder.; Current boundary tests cover capture invocation, caller-provided additional properties, and normal Error stacktrace generation, but do not assert that React `componentStack` is sent. No tests were found for `setupReactErrorHandler`.
- Fix assessment: The missing data is explicitly available at both call sites, and captureException already supports additional properties. The change can remain confined to @posthog/react plus focused regression tests.
- PR: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/pull/4567

## 2026-08-19T21:30:25.047Z
- Item: issue #4570 — Extract the three duplicated OTLP senders; logs drops batches on 5xx where metrics and traces retry
- Conclusion: Confirmed bug: logs drops batches after exhausted retryable HTTP failures, unlike metrics.
- Labels: team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4570
- Relevant files: `packages/core/src/posthog-core-stateless.ts`, `packages/core/src/logs/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/metrics/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/__tests__/posthog.flush.spec.ts`, `packages/core/src/logs/types.ts`, `packages/core/src/metrics/types.ts`
- Findings: `isPostHogFetchRetryableError` returns true for network errors and HTTP 408, 429, or statuses >=500 in `packages/core/src/posthog-core-stateless.ts`.; Both logs and metrics pass that predicate to `fetchWithRetry`, excluding 413 from internal retries.; After a send failure, `_sendLogsBatch` returns `retry-later` only for `PostHogFetchNetworkError`; retryable HTTP errors therefore fall through to `fatal`.; `_sendMetricsBatch` instead returns `retry-later` for every `isPostHogFetchRetryableError` result, explicitly including exhausted 408/429/5xx failures.; `PostHogLogs._doFlush` preserves queued records only for `retry-later`; it persists queue advancement before throwing for `fatal`, so the logs classification causes data loss.; `PostHogMetrics._doFlush` merges a `retry-later` window back and re-arms its flush timer.; The current repository contains `_sendLogsBatch` and `_sendMetricsBatch`, but no `_sendTracesBatch`, OTLP traces endpoint, or OTLP traces payload type.
- Fix assessment: The divergent outcome classification is directly evidenced and can be corrected with a one-condition change plus narrow sender-level regression tests. A generalized extraction is not required to fix the loss and is unsupported by the current two-sender implementation.
- PR: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/pull/4575

## 2026-08-19T21:31:54.959Z
- Item: issue #4571 — Logs OTLP encoder emits int64 as a JSON number instead of a string
- Conclusion: Confirmed OTLP/HTTP JSON encoding bug affecting log and metric attribute integers.
- Labels: team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4571
- Relevant files: `packages/core/src/logs/logs-utils.ts`, `packages/core/src/logs/logs-utils.spec.ts`, `packages/core/src/metrics/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/metrics/index.spec.ts`, `packages/types/src/capture-log.ts`
- Findings: `packages/core/src/logs/logs-utils.ts` handles every finite `Number.isInteger(value)` as `{ intValue: value }`, so the serialized OTLP JSON contains a numeric int64 field.; `packages/core/src/metrics/index.ts` imports and uses `toOtlpKeyValueList()` when creating metric data-point attributes, so the same encoding affects metric attributes but not `asDouble` metric values.; `packages/types/src/capture-log.ts` currently declares `OtlpAnyValue.intValue?: number`, which must be changed along with the encoder for the corrected wire shape.; `packages/core/src/logs/logs-utils.spec.ts` asserts numeric `intValue` for scalar integers, arrays, and key-value lists; `packages/core/src/metrics/index.spec.ts` asserts `{ intValue: 2 }` for a metric attribute.; The existing encoder already correctly represents non-finite numbers as string values, and its object-to-JSON-string behavior is explicitly documented as deliberate; neither needs to be broadened as part of this fix.; No `packages/core/src/traces/otlp.ts` or core traces encoder exists in the inspected checkout, so the issue's claimed traces precedent could not be verified.
- Fix assessment: The faulty behavior is centralized in one shared encoder and has focused unit-test coverage. The change is small, but it alters a shipped OTLP JSON contract for logs and metric attributes, so an ingestion-level verification is needed.

## 2026-08-19T21:33:01.495Z
- Item: issue #4574 — `posthog-react-native/expo`: fix iOS dSYM build ordering and EAS versions
- Conclusion: Confirmed Expo iOS symbol-upload integration bug affecting build ordering and release-version attribution with EAS remote versioning.
- Labels: react-native, feature/error-tracking, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4574
- Relevant files: `packages/react-native/src/tooling/expoconfig.ts`, `packages/react-native/tooling/posthog-xcode.sh`, `packages/react-native/test/expoconfig.spec.ts`, `packages/react-native/test/posthog-xcode-parse.spec.ts`, `packages/react-native/CHANGELOG.md`
- Findings: `addDsymUploadBuildPhase` creates the `Upload PostHog Debug Symbols` PBXShellScriptBuildPhase with `addBuildPhase([], ...)` and only supplies `shellPath` and `shellScript`; it does not supply an `inputPaths` entry for `$(DWARF_DSYM_FOLDER_PATH)/$(DWARF_DSYM_FILE_NAME)/Contents/Resources/DWARF/$(EXECUTABLE_NAME)`.; The dSYM phase being appended last is not equivalent to a declared Xcode dependency, so it does not ensure the dSYM executable is complete before the upload script reads it.; `packages/react-native/tooling/posthog-xcode.sh` constructs `CLI_RELEASE_ARGS` from `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`, `MARKETING_VERSION`, and `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`; it has no `INFOPLIST_FILE` lookup. This directly permits uploads under generated `1.0+1` values when EAS remote versioning updates the plist instead.; The generated dSYM phase invokes posthog-ios's `upload-symbols.sh` without correcting the inherited version/build environment, so it is susceptible to the same stale Xcode build-setting values.; When an existing plugin-generated dSYM phase is found, the plugin currently refreshes only `shellScript`. A fix must also update its input paths, otherwise checked-in native projects will retain the missing dependency after upgrading until the phase is migrated.; Existing unit tests cover shell-script generation and phase idempotency, but do not assert dSYM input paths or release-version resolution from an Expo Info.plist.
- Fix assessment: The affected code is localized to the Expo config plugin and its generated iOS scripts. The report provides the required dSYM dependency path and a concrete EAS remote-version scenario; focused regression tests can cover generated PBX phase input paths and plist-derived release arguments without changing runtime SDK behavior.

## 2026-08-21T10:13:24.867Z
- Item: issue #4595 — Session replay (React Native): support v2 trigger groups (conditional recording)
- Conclusion: Confirmed feature gap: React Native supports legacy conditional-recording fields but does not evaluate the v2 trigger-group configuration.
- Labels: feature, feature/replay, feature/mobile, react-native, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4595
- Relevant files: `packages/react-native/src/posthog-rn.ts`, `packages/react-native/test/session-replay-event-triggers.spec.ts`, `packages/react-native/src/optional/OptionalPlugin.ts`, `packages/react-native/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/browser-common/src/types/remote-config.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/recording-strategies.ts`, `packages/browser/playwright/mocked/session-recording/trigger-groups-v2.spec.ts`, `.agents/skills/replay-incident-risk/INCIDENTS.md`
- Findings: React Native's replay evaluator reads only legacy `linkedFlag` and `eventTriggers` from persisted `SessionReplay` configuration. It has no `version === 2` or `triggerGroups` handling.; The RN event-trigger implementation stores one activated-session value and AND-combines all legacy conditions. It cannot represent multiple independent groups, each with its own match type, sampling decision, activation state, or minimum duration.; RN 4.52.0 released legacy event-trigger support in PR #3932, including session re-arming and linked-flag combination, but this is not v2 trigger-group support.; The browser remote-config schema defines v2 groups with `id`, `name`, `sampleRate`, optional `minDurationMs`, and event, URL, flag, and property conditions. Browser's v2 strategy persists sampling per group and registers replay debug properties.; No React Native implementation was found for v2 trigger-group parsing, group-level sampling, group minimum duration, URL/screen matching, property filtering, or replay debug properties.; The optional RN native plugin bridge exposes recording controls but no v2 trigger-group API, so JS/native responsibilities and minimum-duration support must be explicitly agreed before changing behavior.; This is a recording-start-condition and remote-config change. The replay incident guidance identifies these paths as capable of silently suppressing recordings or changing fleet-wide recording volume; failure behavior for absent, malformed, and delayed v2 config must be deliberate and tested.
- Fix assessment: The current legacy gate is localized, but v2 requires a state model for multiple independently sampled and activated groups, persistence across session changes, screen/URL semantics, duration handling, diagnostics, and coordination with the native replay SDKs. A direct field parser would not safely preserve the required semantics.

## 2026-08-21T12:31:47.093Z
- Item: issue #4596 — @posthog/rollup-plugin 1.4.9+ silently skips Vite 8 client sourcemaps after Oxc strips chunkId comments
- Conclusion: Confirmed regression in the Rollup plugin’s post-1.4.8 in-memory chunk-ID flow when a downstream minifier removes the injected comment.
- Labels: feature/error-tracking, team/error-tracking
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4596
- Relevant files: `packages/rollup-plugin/src/index.ts`, `packages/rollup-plugin/src/index.spec.ts`, `packages/plugin-utils/src/chunk-ids.ts`, `packages/plugin-utils/src/chunk-ids.spec.ts`, `packages/rollup-plugin/CHANGELOG.md`
- Findings: `packages/rollup-plugin/src/index.ts` injects `createChunkIdSnippet(...)` and `createChunkIdComment(...)` in `renderChunk`, but `writeBundle` skips a JavaScript chunk unless `determineChunkIdFromSource(chunk.code)` succeeds.; `packages/plugin-utils/src/chunk-ids.ts` only recognizes a line-anchored `//# chunkId=` comment. Its documentation and test explicitly state that the executable chunk-ID IIFE alone must return `undefined`.; The `writeBundle` empty-selection path emits the same `No chunks found, skipping sourcemap processing` message reported in the issue.; Existing Rollup-plugin tests invoke `renderChunk` and `writeBundle` directly using code that still contains the comment; they do not simulate downstream output minification or run a Vite build.; `packages/rollup-plugin/CHANGELOG.md` records version 1.4.9 / PR #4512 as the release that moved chunk-ID injection into `renderChunk`, matching the reported regression boundary.; The chunk-ID helper documents the comment as the marker posthog-cli discovers at upload time. This means changing only the Rollup-plugin selection condition may be insufficient unless the CLI upload protocol can also derive the ID from the surviving runtime snippet.
- Fix assessment: The immediate gate is localized, but the removed comment is documented as the CLI upload-time chunk-ID protocol and the current filter intentionally avoids including untouched prebuilt chunks. A safe repair requires verifying or extending the shared plugin/CLI identification protocol, rather than broadly uploading all JavaScript chunks or making an unverified IIFE matcher.

## 2026-08-22T14:06:42.227Z
- Item: issue #4599 — React Native Android: proguard mapping upload fails on CI — posthog-cli in node_modules/.bin is never found
- Conclusion: Confirmed integration bug: Android native-symbol uploads use the external Gradle plugin's CLI resolver, which is separate from the React Native SDK's local CLI resolver.
- Labels: Android, react-native, feature/error-tracking, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4599
- Relevant files: `packages/react-native/src/tooling/expoconfig.ts`, `packages/react-native/tooling/posthog.gradle`, `packages/react-native/test/expoconfig.spec.ts`, `packages/react-native/CHANGELOG.md`
- Findings: When uploadNativeSymbols is enabled, the Expo config plugin injects `com.posthog:posthog-android-gradle-plugin:1.4.0` and applies `com.posthog.android` to the app module.; The Expo config plugin only adds the external plugin classpath and apply line; it does not configure `PostHogCliExecTask` or set `postHogExecutable`.; `packages/react-native/tooling/posthog.gradle` has an independent resolver for Hermes sourcemap uploads. It first uses Node `require.resolve('@posthog/cli/package.json')`, then checks `reactRoot/node_modules/@posthog/cli`, and finally checks `reactRoot/node_modules/.bin/posthog-cli` before falling back to a global command.; That local resolver is used only by the React Native SDK's Hermes clone/upload tasks. It does not configure the external Gradle plugin task responsible for `uploadPostHogProguardMappingsRelease`.; The currently inspected Expo integration still pins the Android Gradle plugin to 1.4.0, and the React Native changelog does not document a later local-CLI resolution fix for its ProGuard mapping task.
- Fix assessment: The failing resolver is owned by the separately maintained `posthog-android-gradle-plugin`, not by code in this repository. A durable fix should be implemented and tested there across npm/yarn/pnpm and platform launcher behavior, then consumed here by bumping the injected plugin version. Adding an Expo-only task override in this repository would duplicate resolver behavior and would not address non-Expo React Native integrations.
